subject: humanities
passage: The vivid blue on much Chinese blue-and-white porcelain of the early Ming dynasty (1368–1644) came from cobalt imported from Persia. This imported cobalt contained very little manganese and fired to a bright, sapphire-like blue. Cobalt mined in China, by contrast, was rich in manganese, which gave the blue a duller, grayish tone. Historical records indicate that supplies of Persian cobalt were interrupted during certain decades. A specialist examining an undated Ming piece with a grayish blue might therefore reasonably conclude that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the piece must have been made outside China by Persian potters.
choices.B: the piece may have been made when imported cobalt was scarce.
choices.C: the piece was fired at a lower temperature than other Ming wares.
choices.D: the piece contains more Persian cobalt than bright blue pieces do.

explanation.why: A grayish blue points to manganese-rich Chinese cobalt rather than imported Persian cobalt. Since Persian supplies were sometimes interrupted, a piece colored with local cobalt may date from one of those periods.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The grayish tone points to cobalt mined in China, not to Persian potters working elsewhere.
explanation.B: Correct. Grayish blue suggests local cobalt, which potters would likely have used when Persian imports were cut off.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text explains color by the cobalt's manganese content; firing temperature is never discussed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Persian cobalt produced the bright blue, so a grayish piece likely contains less of it, not more.
